智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires Video-LLMs to decide when to respond as a video unfolds, a task where existing methods often fall short due to their implicit, query-agnostic modeling of visual evidence. We introduce Response-G1, a novel framework that establishes explicit, structured alignment between the accumulated video evidence and the query's expected response conditions via scene graphs. The framework operates in three fine-tuning-free stages: (1) online query-guided scene graph generation from streaming clips; (2) memory-based retrieval of the most semantically relevant historical scene graphs; and (3) retrieval-augmented trigger prompting for per-frame "silence/response" this http URL grounding both evidence and conditions in a shared graph representation, Response-G1 achieves more interpretable and accurate response timing decisions. Experimental results on established benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method in both proactive and reactive tasks, validating the advantage of explicit scene graph modeling and retrieval in streaming video understanding.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: VISD: Enhancing Video Reasoning via Structured Self-Distillation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Hao Lin, Kunyang Lv, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian, Zhongjing Du
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: VISD enhances video reasoning by integrating structured self-distillation with reinforcement learning, improving accuracy and efficiency through fine-grained feedback and robust optimization techniques.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Training VideoLLMs for complex reasoning remains challenging due to sparse sequence level rewards and the lack of fine grained credit assignment over long, temporally grounded reasoning trajectories. While reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision, it fails to capture token level contributions, leading to inefficient learning. Conversely, existing self distillation methods offer dense supervision but lack structure and diagnostic specificity, and often interact unstably with reinforcement learning. In this work, we propose VISD, a structured self distillation framework that introduces diagnostically meaningful privileged information for video reasoning. VISD employs a video aware judge model to decompose reasoning quality into multiple dimensions, including answer correctness, logical consistency, and spatio-temporal grounding, and uses this structured feedback to guide a teacher policy for token level supervision. To stably integrate dense supervision with RL, we introduce a direction magnitude decoupling mechanism, where rollout level advantages computed from rewards determine update direction, while structured privileged signals modulate token level update magnitudes. This design enables semantically aligned and fine grained credit assignment, improving both reasoning faithfulness and training efficiency. Additionally, VISD incorporates curriculum scheduling and EMA based teacher stabilization to support robust optimization over long video sequences. Experiments on diverse benchmarks show that VISD consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving answer accuracy and spatio temporal grounding quality. Notably, VISD reaches these gains with nearly 2x faster convergence in optimization steps, highlighting the effectiveness of structured self supervision in improving both performance and sample efficiency for VideoLLMs.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: DGPO: Distribution Guided Policy Optimization for Fine Grained Credit Assignment
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Hongbo Jin, Rongpeng Zhu, Zhongjing Du, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: DGPO introduces a critic-free reinforcement learning framework that enhances fine-grained credit assignment in language models by using bounded Hellinger distance and entropy gating for improved exploration.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning is crucial for aligning large language models to perform complex reasoning tasks. However, current algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization suffer from coarse grained, sequence level credit assignment, which severely struggles to isolate pivotal reasoning steps within long Chain of Thought generations. Furthermore, the standard unbounded Kullback Leibler divergence penalty induces severe gradient instability and mode seeking conservatism, ultimately stifling the discovery of novel reasoning trajectories. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Distribution Guided Policy Optimization, a novel critic free reinforcement learning framework that reinterprets distribution deviation as a guiding signal rather than a rigid penalty. DGPO replaces the volatile KL divergence with the bounded Hellinger distance to safely quantify token level exploration without the risk of gradient explosion. To effectively distinguish genuine reasoning breakthroughs from hallucinatory noise, we propose an entropy gating mechanism that scales this deviation by the policy`s epistemic uncertainty. By dynamically redistributing the coarse sequence-level advantage to individual tokens based on these gated scores, DGPO heavily incentivizes critical exploratory steps while suppressing unwarranted, low-entropy deviations. Consequently, DGPO completely eliminates the traditional token-level KL penalty and achieves fine-grained credit reallocation without the computational overhead of an additional value network. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that DGPO sets a new state-of-the-art for critic free alignment. Notably, on the Qwen2.5-32B architecture, DGPO achieves 60.0% Avg@32 accuracy and 46.0% Avg@32 accuracy on the challenging AIME2024 and AIME2025 benchmarks respectively, substantially outperforming competitive baselines like DAPO.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Sword: Style-Robust World Models as Simulators via Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping for VLA Policy Post-Training
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Jiaxuan Gao, Yongjian Guo, Zhong Guan, Wen Huang, Wanlun Ma
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The Sword framework enhances World Models for Vision-Language-Action tasks by improving generalization and robustness through Structure-Guided Style Augmentation and Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: The integration of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with World Models has gained increasing attention. One representative approach treats learned World Models as generative simulators, enabling policy optimization entirely within "imagination." However, when deployed as simulators for specific environments such as the LIBERO benchmark, existing World Models often suffer from poor generalization and long-horizon error accumulation. During closed-loop rollouts, these models are highly sensitive to initial-state perturbations; minor changes in color, illumination, and other visual factors can trigger cascading hallucinations, leading to severe blurriness or overexposure. Moreover, long-horizon error accumulation further degrades the quality and fidelity of predicted future states. These issues limit the reliability of World Models as simulators. To mitigate these problems, we propose Sword, a robust World Model framework. Our method introduces Structure-Guided Style Augmentation to disentangle the visual textures of interactive environments from task-relevant dynamics, thereby improving generalization. We further propose Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping, which maintains consistency between training and inference while keeping memory consumption low. Extensive experiments on the LIBERO benchmark show that our method significantly outperforms the baseline WoVR in terms of generalization, generation quality, robustness, fidelity, and the success rate of reinforcement-learning post-training for VLA models.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: VLA-GSE: Boosting Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning in VLA with Generalized and Specialized Experts
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yuhua Jiang, Junjie Lu, Xinyao Qin, Xiaoyu Chen, Kaixin Wang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: VLA-GSE enhances parameter-efficient fine-tuning for vision-language-action models by using generalized and specialized experts, improving robotic control adaptation while preserving pre-trained knowledge.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models inherit rich visual-semantic priors from pre-trained vision-language backbones, but adapting them to robotic control remains challenging. Full fine-tuning (FFT) is prone to overfitting on downstream robotic data and catastrophic forgetting of pretrained vision-language capabilities. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) better preserves pre-trained knowledge, yet existing PEFT methods still struggle to adapt effectively to robot control tasks. To address this gap, we propose VLA-GSE, a parameter-efficient VLA fine-tuning framework that improves control adaptation while retaining PEFT's knowledge preservation advantage. Specifically, VLA-GSE (Generalized and Specialized Experts) is initialized by spectrally decomposing the frozen backbone, assigning leading singular components to generalized experts (shared experts) and disjoint residual components to specialized experts (routed experts). This decomposition improves adaptation capacity under a fixed trainable-parameter budget. Under a comparable parameter budget, VLA-GSE updates only 2.51% of the full model parameters and consistently outperforms strong FFT and PEFT baselines. It achieves 81.2% average zero-shot success on LIBERO-Plus, preserves pre-trained VLM capability comparably to LoRA on multimodal understanding benchmarks, and improves real-world manipulation success under multiple distribution shifts. Code is available at: this https URL

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Beyond LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning: Gradient-Guided Optimizer Routing for LLM Adaptation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Haozhan Tang, Xiuqi Zhu, Xinyin Zhang, Boxun Li, Virginia Smith
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper introduces Mixture of LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning (MoLF), a dynamic framework that optimally combines FFT and LoRA for improved large language model adaptation.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Recent literature on fine-tuning Large Language Models highlights a fundamental debate. While Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) provides the representational plasticity required for high-entropy knowledge injection, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can match or surpass FFT performance because many tasks only require updates in a low-rank space and benefit from LoRA's additional regularization. Through empirical evaluation across diverse tasks (SQL, Medical QA, and Counterfactual Knowledge) and varying language models (Gemma-3-1B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-3B), we verify both trends and demonstrate that relying solely on either static architecture is structurally limited. To address this challenge, we propose a Mixture of LoRA and Full (MoLF) Fine-Tuning, a unified framework that enables continuous navigation between both training regimes. MoLF dynamically routes updates between FFT and LoRA at the optimizer level to ensure that exact gradient signals are available to both experts throughout training, yielding stable training dynamics. For memory-constrained environments, we also introduce MoLF-Efficient, which freezes base weights and only routes updates among a pair of LoRA experts of potentially varying rank. Our evaluations show that MoLF either improves on or stays within $1.5\%$ of the better of FFT and LoRA across all settings, while MoLF-Efficient outperforms prior adaptive LoRA approaches by up to $20\%$ on Fact and $9\%$ on Med and SQL.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: AEM: Adaptive Entropy Modulation for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Haotian Zhao, Songlin Zhou, Yuxin Zhang, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Wenyu Zhang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: AEM introduces a supervision-free method for credit assignment in multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning by adaptively modulating entropy dynamics, enhancing exploration-exploitation balance and improving performance across various tasks.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the ability of large language model (LLM) agents to interact with environments and solve multi-turn tasks. However, effective agentic RL remains challenging: sparse outcome-only rewards provide limited guidance for assigning credit to individual steps within long interaction trajectories. Existing approaches often introduce dense intermediate supervision, such as process reward models or auxiliary self-supervised signals, which increases supervision and tuning complexity and may limit generalization across tasks and domains. We present AEM, a supervision-free credit assignment method that adaptively modulates entropy dynamics during RL training to improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off. Since in agentic RL the environment is typically affected by a complete response, rather than an individual token, our analysis lifts entropy dynamics from the token level to the response level, aligning uncertainty estimation with the effective action granularity of LLM agents and reducing sensitivity to token-level sampling noise. We further show that entropy drift under natural-gradient updates is governed by the interaction between the sampled-response advantage and its relative surprisal. Motivated by this result, AEM derives a practical response-level uncertainty proxy and uses it to rescale advantages, leveraging the evolving balance between positive and negative samples to naturally transition from exploration to exploitation. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SWE-bench-Verified with models ranging from 1.5B to 32B demonstrate that AEM consistently improves strong RL baselines, including a +1.4\% gain when integrated into a state-of-the-art software-engineering RL training framework.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Proxy3D: Efficient 3D Representations for Vision-Language Models via Semantic Clustering and Alignment
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jerry Jiang, Haowen Sun, Denis Gudovskiy, Yohei Nakata, Tomoyuki Okuno
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: Proxy3D introduces efficient 3D proxy representations for vision-language models, enhancing spatial consistency and performance in 3D visual tasks through semantic clustering and alignment.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence in vision-language models (VLMs) attracts research interest with the practical demand to reason in the 3D this http URL promising results, most existing methods follow the conventional 2D pipeline in VLMs and use pixel-aligned representations for the vision modality. However, correspondence-based models with implicit 3D scene understanding often fail to achieve spatial consistency, and representation-based models with 3D geometric priors lack efficiency in vision sequence serialization. To address this, we propose a Proxy3D method with compact yet comprehensive 3D proxy representations for the vision modality. Given only video frames as input, we employ semantic and geometric encoders to extract scene features and then perform their semantic-aware clustering to obtain a set of proxies in the 3D space. For representation alignment, we further curate the SpaceSpan dataset and apply multi-stage training to adopt the proposed 3D proxy representations with the VLM. When using shorter sequences for vision information, our method achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance in 3D visual question answering, visual grounding and general spatial intelligence benchmarks.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Towards Highly-Constrained Human Motion Generation with Retrieval-Guided Diffusion Noise Optimization
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Hanchao Liu, Fang-Lue Zhang, Shining Zhang, Tai-Jiang Mu, Shi-Min Hu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: This paper presents a retrieval-guided diffusion noise optimization method for generating human motion that effectively addresses complex spatiotemporal constraints without prior training.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Generating human motion that satisfies customized zero-shot goal functions, enabling applications such as controllable character animation and behavior synthesis for virtual agents, is a critical capability. While current approaches handle many unseen constraints, they fail on tasks with very challenging spatiotemporal restrictions, such as severe spatial obstacles or specified numbers of walking steps. To equip motion generators for these highly constrained tasks, we present a retrieval-guided method built on the training-free diffusion noise optimization framework. The key idea is to search within large motion datasets for guidance that can potentially satisfy difficult constraints. We introduce relational task parsing to group target constraints and identify the difficult ones to be handled by retrieved reference. A better initialization for diffusion noise is then obtained via a reward-guided mask that combines random noise with retrieved noise. By optimizing diffusion noise from this improved initialization, we successfully solve highly constrained generation tasks. By leveraging LLM for relational task parsing, the whole framework is further enabled to automatically reason for what to retrieve, improving the intelligence of moving agents under a training-free optimization scheme.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: NoiseGate: Learning Per-Latent Timestep Schedules as Information Gating in World Action Models
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Wen Huang, Haoran Sun, Yongjian Guo, Yunxuan Ma, Haoran Li
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: NoiseGate introduces a learnable information-gating policy for World Action Models, enhancing action generation by assigning independent timesteps to latent frames during training.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) are an emerging family of policies that tie robot action generation to future-observation modeling. In this work, we focus on the joint video--action modeling paradigm, where actions and imagined future observations are co-generated along a shared denoising or flow trajectory, so that perception, prediction, and control are coupled within one generative process. Existing WAMs typically realize this paradigm with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT), where video and action tokens interact through shared self-attention. This architecture can in principle assign a separate timestep $t_f$ to each predicted latent frame, yet current systems collapse this degree of freedom onto a single shared scalar $t$. Under the noise-as-masking view of Diffusion Forcing, this shared schedule imposes the unjustified prior that every predicted latent is equally reliable for action generation. We instead view the per-latent schedule as a \emph{learnable information-gating policy}: by changing a latent frame's noise level, the policy modulates the reliability of its Key/Value contribution to the action tokens. We propose \textbf{NoiseGate}, which combines independent per-latent timestep sampling during backbone training, a lightweight Gating Policy Network that emits per-latent time increments during denoising, and task-reward optimization that trains the schedule policy without hand-crafted shape priors. Built on a joint video--action MoT backbone, NoiseGate delivers consistent gains on diverse RoboTwin random-scene manipulation tasks.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: BrickCraft: Visuomotor Skill Composition with Situated Manual Guidance for Long-Horizon Interlocking Brick Assembly
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jichuan Yu, Bowei Li, Zhenran Tang, Guanxing Lu, Chuxiong Hu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: BrickCraft is a framework that enables robots to autonomously assemble interlocking bricks by integrating long-horizon task reasoning with spatially guided visuomotor skills.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Autonomous robotic assembly of interlocking bricks demands seamless integration of long-horizon task reasoning, spatial grounding, and fine-grained manipulation. This paper presents BrickCraft, a compositional framework designed for long-horizon and generalizable interlocking brick assembly. BrickCraft models the assembly process using a relative formulation, where each step is anchored to a reference brick within the partial structure, thereby decomposing complex tasks into a finite set of reusable primitive skills. BrickCraft bridges the gap between high-level assembly plans and physical execution through situated manuals, which provide explicit spatial guidance for learned visuomotor skills by projecting the assembly intent onto real-time robot observations. Finally, BrickCraft employs a compositional execution pipeline that chains these spatially grounded skills to accomplish long-horizon assembly tasks. Extensive experimental validations demonstrate that BrickCraft acquires proficient assembly skills from a limited set of demonstrations and exhibits strong compositional generalization to unseen structures. The project website is available at this https URL.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: SAM 3D Animal: Promptable Animal 3D Reconstruction from Images in the Wild
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Xuyi Hu, Jin Lyu, Jiuming Liu, Yebin Liu, Silvia Zuffi
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: SAM 3D Animal introduces a promptable framework for multi-animal 3D reconstruction from single images, leveraging a new dataset and achieving state-of-the-art performance.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: 3D animal reconstruction in the wild remains challenging due to large species variation, frequent occlusions, and the prevalence of multi-animal scenes, while existing methods predominantly focus on single-animal settings. We present SAM 3D Animal, the first promptable framework for multi-animal 3D reconstruction from a single image. Built on the SMAL+ parametric animal model, our method jointly reconstructs multiple instances and supports flexible prompts in the form of keypoints and masks which enable more reliable disambiguation in crowded and occluded scenes. To train such a model, we further introduce Herd3D, a multi-animal 3D dataset containing over 5K images, designed to increase diversity in species, interactions, and occlusion patterns. Experiments on the Animal3D, APTv2, and Animal Kingdom datasets show that our framework achieves state-of-the-art results over both existing model-based and model-free methods, demonstrating a scalable and effective solution for prompt-driven animal 3D reconstruction in the wild.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: MemCompiler: Compile, Don't Inject -- State-Conditioned Memory for Embodied Agents
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Xin Ding, Xinrui Wang, Yifan Yang, Hao Wu, Shiqi Jiang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: MemCompiler enhances embodied agents by dynamically compiling relevant memory based on current state, significantly improving performance and efficiency compared to traditional static memory systems.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Existing memory systems for embodied agents typically inject retrieved memory as static context at episode start, a paradigm we term Ahead-of-time Monolithic Memory Injection (AMMI). However, this static design quickly becomes misaligned with the agent's evolving state and may degrade lightweight executors below the no-memory baseline. To address this, we propose MemCompiler, which reframes memory utilization as State-Conditioned Memory Compilation. A learned Memory Compiler reads a structured Brief State capturing the agent's current execution state and dynamically selects and compiles only relevant memory into executable guidance. This guidance is delivered through a text channel and a latent Soft-Mem channel that preserves perceptual information not expressible in text. Across Alf World, EmbodiedBench, and ScienceWorld, MemCompiler consistently improves over no-memory across open-source backbones (up to +129%), matches or approaches frontier closed-source systems, and reduces per-step latency by 60%, demonstrating that state-aware memory compilation improves both effectiveness and efficiency.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Beyond LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning: Gradient-Guided Optimizer Routing for LLM Adaptation
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Haozhan Tang, Xiuqi Zhu, Xinyin Zhang, Boxun Li, Virginia Smith
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces Mixture of LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning (MoLF), a dynamic framework that optimally combines FFT and LoRA for improved large language model adaptation.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Recent literature on fine-tuning Large Language Models highlights a fundamental debate. While Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) provides the representational plasticity required for high-entropy knowledge injection, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can match or surpass FFT performance because many tasks only require updates in a low-rank space and benefit from LoRA's additional regularization. MoLF dynamically routes updates between FFT and LoRA at the optimizer level to ensure that exact gradient signals are available to both experts throughout training, yielding stable training dynamics. 智能技术与系统实验室.title: AEM: Adaptive Entropy Modulation for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Haotian Zhao, Songlin Zhou, Yuxin Zhang, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Wenyu Zhang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: AEM introduces a supervision-free method for credit assignment in multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning by adaptively modulating entropy dynamics, enhancing exploration-exploitation balance and improving performance across various tasks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the ability of large language model (LLM) agents to interact with environments and solve multi-turn tasks. However, effective agentic RL remains challenging: sparse outcome-only rewards provide limited guidance for assigning credit to individual steps within long interaction trajectories. Existing approaches often introduce dense intermediate supervision, such as process reward models or auxiliary self-supervised signals, which increases supervision and tuning complexity and may limit generalization across tasks and domains. We present AEM, a supervision-free credit assignment method that adaptively modulates entropy dynamics during RL training to improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off. Since in agentic RL the environment is typically affected by a complete response, rather than an individual token, our analysis lifts entropy dynamics from the token level to the response level, aligning uncertainty estimation with the effective action granularity of LLM agents and reducing sensitivity to token-level sampling noise. We further show that entropy drift under natural-gradient updates is governed by the interaction between the sampled-response advantage and its relative surprisal. Motivated by this result, AEM derives a practical response-level uncertainty proxy and uses it to rescale advantages, leveraging the evolving balance between positive and negative samples to naturally transition from exploration to exploitation. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SWE-bench-Verified with models ranging from 1.5B to 32B demonstrate that AEM consistently improves strong RL baselines, including a +1.4\% gain when integrated into a state-of-the-art software-engineering RL training framework.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Proxy3D: Efficient 3D Representations for Vision-Language Models via Semantic Clustering and Alignment
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Jerry Jiang, Haowen Sun, Denis Gudovskiy, Yohei Nakata, Tomoyuki Okuno
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: Proxy3D introduces efficient 3D proxy representations for vision-language models, enhancing spatial consistency and performance in 3D visual tasks through semantic clustering and alignment.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence in vision-language models (VLMs) attracts research interest with the practical demand to reason in the 3D this http URL promising results, most existing methods follow the conventional 2D pipeline in VLMs and use pixel-aligned representations for the vision modality. However, correspondence-based models with implicit 3D scene understanding often fail to achieve spatial consistency, and representation-based models with 3D geometric priors lack efficiency in vision sequence serialization. To address this, we propose a Proxy3D method with compact yet comprehensive 3D proxy representations for the vision modality. Given only video frames as input, we employ semantic and geometric encoders to extract scene features and then perform their semantic-aware clustering to obtain a set of proxies in the 3D space. For representation alignment, we further curate the SpaceSpan dataset and apply multi-stage training to adopt the proposed 3D proxy representations with the VLM. When using shorter sequences for vision information, our method achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance in 3D visual question answering, visual grounding and general spatial intelligence benchmarks.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Towards Highly-Constrained Human Motion Generation with Retrieval-Guided Diffusion Noise Optimization
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Hanchao Liu, Fang-Lue Zhang, Shining Zhang, Tai-Jiang Mu, Shi-Min Hu
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: This paper presents a retrieval-guided diffusion noise optimization method for generating human motion that effectively addresses complex spatiotemporal constraints without prior training.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Generating human motion that satisfies customized zero-shot goal functions, enabling applications such as controllable character animation and behavior synthesis for virtual agents, is a critical capability. While current approaches handle many unseen constraints, they fail on tasks with very challenging spatiotemporal restrictions, such as severe spatial obstacles or specified numbers of walking steps. To equip motion generators for these highly constrained tasks, we present a retrieval-guided method built on the training-free diffusion noise optimization framework. The key idea is to search within large motion datasets for guidance that can potentially satisfy difficult constraints. We introduce relational task parsing to group target constraints and identify the difficult ones to be handled by retrieved reference. A better initialization for diffusion noise is then obtained via a reward-guided mask that combines random noise with retrieved noise. By optimizing diffusion noise from this improved initialization, we successfully solve highly constrained generation tasks. By leveraging LLM for relational task parsing, the whole framework is further enabled to automatically reason for what to retrieve, improving the intelligence of moving agents under a training-free optimization scheme.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: NoiseGate: Learning Per-Latent Timestep Schedules as Information Gating in World Action Models
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Wen Huang, Haoran Sun, Yongjian Guo, Yunxuan Ma, Haoran Li
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: NoiseGate introduces a learnable information-gating policy for World Action Models, enhancing action generation by assigning independent timesteps to latent frames during training.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) are an emerging family of policies that tie robot action generation to future-observation modeling. In this work, we focus on the joint video--action modeling paradigm, where actions and imagined future observations are co-generated along a shared denoising or flow trajectory, so that perception, prediction, and control are coupled within one generative process. Existing WAMs typically realize this paradigm with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT), where video and action tokens interact through shared self-attention. This architecture can in principle assign a separate timestep $t_f$ to each predicted latent frame, yet current systems collapse this degree of freedom onto a single shared scalar $t$. Under the noise-as-masking view of Diffusion Forcing, this shared schedule imposes the unjustified prior that every predicted latent is equally reliable for action generation. We instead view the per-latent schedule as a \emph{learnable information-gating policy}: by changing a latent frame's noise level, the policy modulates the reliability of its Key/Value contribution to the action tokens. We propose \textbf{NoiseGate}, which combines independent per-latent timestep sampling during backbone training, a lightweight Gating Policy Network that emits per-latent time increments during denoising, and task-reward optimization that trains the schedule policy without hand-crafted shape priors. Built on a joint video--action MoT backbone, NoiseGate delivers consistent gains on diverse RoboTwin random-scene manipulation tasks.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: BrickCraft: Visuomotor Skill Composition with Situated Manual Guidance for Long-Horizon Interlocking Brick Assembly
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Jichuan Yu, Bowei Li, Zhenran Tang, Guanxing Lu, Chuxiong Hu
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: BrickCraft is a framework that enables robots to autonomously assemble interlocking bricks by integrating long-horizon task reasoning with spatially guided visuomotor skills.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Autonomous robotic assembly of interlocking bricks demands seamless integration of long-horizon task reasoning, spatial grounding, and fine-grained manipulation. This paper presents BrickCraft, a compositional framework designed for long-horizon and generalizable interlocking brick assembly. BrickCraft models the assembly process using a relative formulation, where each step is anchored to a reference brick within the partial structure, thereby decomposing complex tasks into a finite set of reusable primitive skills. BrickCraft bridges the gap between high-level assembly plans and physical execution through situated manuals, which provide explicit spatial guidance for learned visuomotor skills by projecting the assembly intent onto real-time robot observations. Finally, BrickCraft employs a compositional execution pipeline that chains these spatially grounded skills to accomplish long-horizon assembly tasks. Extensive experimental validations demonstrate that BrickCraft acquires proficient assembly skills from a limited set of demonstrations and exhibits strong compositional generalization to unseen structures. The project website is available at this https URL.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: SAM 3D Animal: Promptable Animal 3D Reconstruction from Images in the Wild
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Xuyi Hu, Jin Lyu, Jiuming Liu, Yebin Liu, Silvia Zuffi
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: SAM 3D Animal introduces a promptable framework for multi-animal 3D reconstruction from single images, leveraging a new dataset and achieving state-of-the-art performance.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: 3D animal reconstruction in the wild remains challenging due to large species variation, frequent occlusions, and the prevalence of multi-animal scenes, while existing methods predominantly focus on single-animal settings. We present SAM 3D Animal, the first promptable framework for multi-animal 3D reconstruction from a single image. Built on the SMAL+ parametric animal model, our method jointly reconstructs multiple instances and supports flexible prompts in the form of keypoints and masks which enable more reliable disambiguation in crowded and occluded scenes. To train such a model, we further introduce Herd3D, a multi-animal 3D dataset containing over 5K images, designed to increase diversity in species, interactions, and occlusion patterns. Experiments on the Animal3D, APTv2, and Animal Kingdom datasets show that our framework achieves state-of-the-art results over both existing model-based and model-free methods, demonstrating a scalable and effective solution for prompt-driven animal 3D reconstruction in the wild.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: MemCompiler: Compile, Don't Inject -- State-Conditioned Memory for Embodied Agents
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Xin Ding, Xinrui Wang, Yifan Yang, Hao Wu, Shiqi Jiang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: MemCompiler enhances embodied agents by dynamically compiling relevant memory based on current state, significantly improving performance and efficiency compared to traditional static memory systems.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Existing memory systems for embodied agents typically inject retrieved memory as static context at episode start, a paradigm we term Ahead-of-time Monolithic Memory Injection (AMMI). However, this static design quickly becomes misaligned with the agent's evolving state and may degrade lightweight executors below the no-memory baseline. To address this, we propose MemCompiler, which reframes memory utilization as State-Conditioned Memory Compilation. A learned Memory Compiler reads a structured Brief State capturing the agent's current execution state and dynamically selects and compiles only relevant memory into executable guidance. This guidance is delivered through a text channel and a latent Soft-Mem channel that preserves perceptual information not expressible in text. Across Alf World, EmbodiedBench, and ScienceWorld, MemCompiler consistently improves over no-memory across open-source backbones (up to +129%), matches or approaches frontier closed-source systems, and reduces per-step latency by 60%, demonstrating that state-aware memory compilation improves both effectiveness and efficiency.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Response-G1: Explicit Scene Graph Modeling for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Ke Ma, Jiaqi Tang, Bin Guo, Xueting Han, Ruonan Xu
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: Response-G1 introduces a structured scene graph framework for proactive video understanding, enhancing response timing accuracy through explicit evidence-query alignment and memory retrieval.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires Video-LLMs to decide when to respond as a video unfolds, a task where existing methods often fall short due to their implicit, query-agnostic modeling of visual evidence. We introduce Response-G1, a novel framework that establishes explicit, structured alignment between the accumulated video evidence and the query's expected response conditions via scene graphs. The framework operates in three fine-tuning-free stages: (1) online query-guided scene graph generation from streaming clips; (2) memory-based retrieval of the most semantically relevant historical scene graphs; and (3) retrieval-augmented trigger prompting for per-frame "silence/response" this http URL grounding both evidence and conditions in a shared graph representation, Response-G1 achieves more interpretable and accurate response timing decisions. Experimental results on established benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method in both proactive and reactive tasks, validating the advantage of explicit scene graph modeling and retrieval in streaming video understanding.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: VISD: Enhancing Video Reasoning via Structured Self-Distillation
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Hao Lin, Kunyang Lv, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian, Zhongjing Du
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: VISD enhances video reasoning by integrating structured self-distillation with reinforcement learning, improving accuracy and efficiency through fine-grained feedback and robust optimization techniques.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Training VideoLLMs for complex reasoning remains challenging due to sparse sequence level rewards and the lack of fine grained credit assignment over long, temporally grounded reasoning trajectories. While reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision, it fails to capture token level contributions, leading to inefficient learning. Conversely, existing self distillation methods offer dense supervision but lack structure and diagnostic specificity, and often interact unstably with reinforcement learning. In this work, we propose VISD, a structured self distillation framework that introduces diagnostically meaningful privileged information for video reasoning. VISD employs a video aware judge model to decompose reasoning quality into multiple dimensions, including answer correctness, logical consistency, and spatio-temporal grounding, and uses this structured feedback to guide a teacher policy for token level supervision. To stably integrate dense supervision with RL, we introduce a direction magnitude decoupling mechanism, where rollout level advantages computed from rewards determine update direction, while structured privileged signals modulate token level update magnitudes. This design enables semantically aligned and fine grained credit assignment, improving both reasoning faithfulness and training efficiency. Additionally, VISD incorporates curriculum scheduling and EMA based teacher stabilization to support robust optimization over long video sequences. Experiments on diverse benchmarks show that VISD consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving answer accuracy and spatio temporal grounding quality. Notably, VISD reaches these gains with nearly 2x faster convergence in optimization steps, highlighting the effectiveness of structured self supervision in improving both performance and sample efficiency for VideoLLMs.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: DGPO: Distribution Guided Policy Optimization for Fine Grained Credit Assignment
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Hongbo Jin, Rongpeng Zhu, Zhongjing Du, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: DGPO introduces a critic-free reinforcement learning framework that enhances fine-grained credit assignment in language models by using bounded Hellinger distance and entropy gating for improved exploration.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning is crucial for aligning large language models to perform complex reasoning tasks. However, current algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization suffer from coarse grained, sequence level credit assignment, which severely struggles to isolate pivotal reasoning steps within long Chain of Thought generations. Furthermore, the standard unbounded Kullback Leibler divergence penalty induces severe gradient instability and mode seeking conservatism, ultimately stifling the discovery of novel reasoning trajectories. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Distribution Guided Policy Optimization, a novel critic free reinforcement learning framework that reinterprets distribution deviation as a guiding signal rather than a rigid penalty. DGPO replaces the volatile KL divergence with the bounded Hellinger distance to safely quantify token level exploration without the risk of gradient explosion. To effectively distinguish genuine reasoning breakthroughs from hallucinatory noise, we propose an entropy gating mechanism that scales this deviation by the policy`s epistemic uncertainty. By dynamically redistributing the coarse sequence-level advantage to individual tokens based on these gated scores, DGPO heavily incentivizes critical exploratory steps while suppressing unwarranted, low-entropy deviations. Consequently, DGPO completely eliminates the traditional token-level KL penalty and achieves fine-grained credit reallocation without the computational overhead of an additional value network. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that DGPO sets a new state-of-the-art for critic free alignment. Notably, on the Qwen2.5-32B architecture, DGPO achieves 60.0% Avg@32 accuracy and 46.0% Avg@32 accuracy on the challenging AIME2024 and AIME2025 benchmarks respectively, substantially outperforming competitive baselines like DAPO.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Sword: Style-Robust World Models as Simulators via Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping for VLA Policy Post-Training
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Jiaxuan Gao, Yongjian Guo, Zhong Guan, Wen Huang, Wanlun Ma
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The Sword framework enhances World Models for Vision-Language-Action tasks by improving generalization and robustness through Structure-Guided Style Augmentation and Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: The integration of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with World Models has gained increasing attention. One representative approach treats learned World Models as generative simulators, enabling policy optimization entirely within "imagination." However, when deployed as simulators for specific environments such as the LIBERO benchmark, existing World Models often suffer from poor generalization and long-horizon error accumulation. During closed-loop rollouts, these models are highly sensitive to initial-state perturbations; minor changes in color, illumination, and other visual factors can trigger cascading hallucinations, leading to severe blurriness or overexposure. Moreover, long-horizon error accumulation further degrades the quality and fidelity of predicted future states. These issues limit the reliability of World Models as simulators. To mitigate these problems, we propose Sword, a robust World Model framework. Our method introduces Structure-Guided Style Augmentation to disentangle the visual textures of interactive environments from task-relevant dynamics, thereby improving generalization. We further propose Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping, which maintains consistency between training and inference while keeping memory consumption low. Extensive experiments on the LIBERO benchmark show that our method significantly outperforms the baseline WoVR in terms of generalization, generation quality, robustness, fidelity, and the success rate of reinforcement-learning post-training for VLA models.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: VLA-GSE: Boosting Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning in VLA with Generalized and Specialized Experts
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Yuhua Jiang, Junjie Lu, Xinyao Qin, Xiaoyu Chen, Kaixin Wang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: VLA-GSE enhances parameter-efficient fine-tuning for vision-language-action models by using generalized and specialized experts, improving robotic control adaptation while preserving pre-trained knowledge.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models inherit rich visual-semantic priors from pre-trained vision-language backbones, but adapting them to robotic control remains challenging. Full fine-tuning (FFT) is prone to overfitting on downstream robotic data and catastrophic forgetting of pretrained vision-language capabilities. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) better preserves pre-trained knowledge, yet existing PEFT methods still struggle to adapt effectively to robot control tasks. To address this gap, we propose VLA-GSE, a parameter-efficient VLA fine-tuning framework that improves control adaptation while retaining PEFT's knowledge preservation advantage. Specifically, VLA-GSE (Generalized and Specialized Experts) is initialized by spectrally decomposing the frozen backbone, assigning leading singular components to generalized experts (shared experts) and disjoint residual components to specialized experts (routed experts). This decomposition improves adaptation capacity under a fixed trainable-parameter budget. Under a comparable parameter budget, VLA-GSE updates only 2.51% of the full model parameters and consistently outperforms strong FFT and PEFT baselines. It achieves 81.2% average zero-shot success on LIBERO-Plus, preserves pre-trained VLM capability comparably to LoRA on multimodal understanding benchmarks, and improves real-world manipulation success under multiple distribution shifts. Finally, BrickCraft employs a compositional execution pipeline that chains these spatially grounded skills to accomplish long-horizon assembly tasks. 具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xuyi Hu, Jin Lyu, Jiuming Liu, Yebin Liu, Silvia Zuffi
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: SAM 3D Animal introduces a promptable framework for multi-animal 3D reconstruction from single images, leveraging a new dataset and achieving state-of-the-art performance.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: MemCompiler: Compile, Don't Inject -- State-Conditioned Memory for Embodied Agents
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xin Ding, Xinrui Wang, Yifan Yang, Hao Wu, Shiqi Jiang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: MemCompiler enhances embodied agents by dynamically compiling relevant memory based on current state, significantly improving performance and efficiency compared to traditional static memory systems.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Existing memory systems for embodied agents typically inject retrieved memory as static context at episode start, a paradigm we term Ahead-of-time Monolithic Memory Injection (AMMI). However, this static design quickly becomes misaligned with the agent's evolving state and may degrade lightweight executors below the no-memory baseline. To address this, we propose MemCompiler, which reframes memory utilization as State-Conditioned Memory Compilation. 具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Response-G1: Explicit Scene Graph Modeling for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Ke Ma, Jiaqi Tang, Bin Guo, Xueting Han, Ruonan Xu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Response-G1 introduces a structured scene graph framework for proactive video understanding, enhancing response timing accuracy through explicit evidence-query alignment and memory retrieval.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires Video-LLMs to decide when to respond as a video unfolds, a task where existing methods often fall short due to their implicit, query-agnostic modeling of visual evidence. We introduce Response-G1, a novel framework that establishes explicit, structured alignment between the accumulated video evidence and the query's expected response conditions via scene graphs. The framework operates in three fine-tuning-free stages: (1) online query-guided scene graph generation from streaming clips; (2) memory-based retrieval of the most semantically relevant historical scene graphs; and (3) retrieval-augmented trigger prompting for per-frame "silence/response" this http URL grounding both evidence and conditions in a shared graph representation, Response-G1 achieves more interpretable and accurate response timing decisions. Experimental results on established benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method in both proactive and reactive tasks, validating the advantage of explicit scene graph modeling and retrieval in streaming video understanding.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: VISD: Enhancing Video Reasoning via Structured Self-Distillation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Hao Lin, Kunyang Lv, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian, Zhongjing Du
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: VISD enhances video reasoning by integrating structured self-distillation with reinforcement learning, improving accuracy and efficiency through fine-grained feedback and robust optimization techniques.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Training VideoLLMs for complex reasoning remains challenging due to sparse sequence level rewards and the lack of fine grained credit assignment over long, temporally grounded reasoning trajectories. While reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision, it fails to capture token level contributions, leading to inefficient learning. Conversely, existing self distillation methods offer dense supervision but lack structure and diagnostic specificity, and often interact unstably with reinforcement learning. In this work, we propose VISD, a structured self distillation framework that introduces diagnostically meaningful privileged information for video reasoning. VISD employs a video aware judge model to decompose reasoning quality into multiple dimensions, including answer correctness, logical consistency, and spatio-temporal grounding, and uses this structured feedback to guide a teacher policy for token level supervision. To stably integrate dense supervision with RL, we introduce a direction magnitude decoupling mechanism, where rollout level advantages computed from rewards determine update direction, while structured privileged signals modulate token level update magnitudes. This design enables semantically aligned and fine grained credit assignment, improving both reasoning faithfulness and training efficiency. Additionally, VISD incorporates curriculum scheduling and EMA based teacher stabilization to support robust optimization over long video sequences. Experiments on diverse benchmarks show that VISD consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving answer accuracy and spatio temporal grounding quality. Notably, VISD reaches these gains with nearly 2x faster convergence in optimization steps, highlighting the effectiveness of structured self supervision in improving both performance and sample efficiency for VideoLLMs.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: DGPO: Distribution Guided Policy Optimization for Fine Grained Credit Assignment
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Hongbo Jin, Rongpeng Zhu, Zhongjing Du, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: DGPO introduces a critic-free reinforcement learning framework that enhances fine-grained credit assignment in language models by using bounded Hellinger distance and entropy gating for improved exploration.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning is crucial for aligning large language models to perform complex reasoning tasks. However, current algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization suffer from coarse grained, sequence level credit assignment, which severely struggles to isolate pivotal reasoning steps within long Chain of Thought generations. Furthermore, the standard unbounded Kullback Leibler divergence penalty induces severe gradient instability and mode seeking conservatism, ultimately stifling the discovery of novel reasoning trajectories. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Distribution Guided Policy Optimization, a novel critic free reinforcement learning framework that reinterprets distribution deviation as a guiding signal rather than a rigid penalty. DGPO replaces the volatile KL divergence with the bounded Hellinger distance to safely quantify token level exploration without the risk of gradient explosion. To effectively distinguish genuine reasoning breakthroughs from hallucinatory noise, we propose an entropy gating mechanism that scales this deviation by the policy`s epistemic uncertainty. By dynamically redistributing the coarse sequence-level advantage to individual tokens based on these gated scores, DGPO heavily incentivizes critical exploratory steps while suppressing unwarranted, low-entropy deviations. Consequently, DGPO completely eliminates the traditional token-level KL penalty and achieves fine-grained credit reallocation without the computational overhead of an additional value network. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that DGPO sets a new state-of-the-art for critic free alignment. Notably, on the Qwen2.5-32B architecture, DGPO achieves 60.0% Avg@32 accuracy and 46.0% Avg@32 accuracy on the challenging AIME2024 and AIME2025 benchmarks respectively, substantially outperforming competitive baselines like DAPO.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Sword: Style-Robust World Models as Simulators via Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping for VLA Policy Post-Training
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Jiaxuan Gao, Yongjian Guo, Zhong Guan, Wen Huang, Wanlun Ma
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The Sword framework enhances World Models for Vision-Language-Action tasks by improving generalization and robustness through Structure-Guided Style Augmentation and Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: The integration of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with World Models has gained increasing attention. One representative approach treats learned World Models as generative simulators, enabling policy optimization entirely within "imagination." However, when deployed as simulators for specific environments such as the LIBERO benchmark, existing World Models often suffer from poor generalization and long-horizon error accumulation. During closed-loop rollouts, these models are highly sensitive to initial-state perturbations; minor changes in color, illumination, and other visual factors can trigger cascading hallucinations, leading to severe blurriness or overexposure. Moreover, long-horizon error accumulation further degrades the quality and fidelity of predicted future states. These issues limit the reliability of World Models as simulators. To mitigate these problems, we propose Sword, a robust World Model framework. Our method introduces Structure-Guided Style Augmentation to disentangle the visual textures of interactive environments from task-relevant dynamics, thereby improving generalization. We further propose Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping, which maintains consistency between training and inference while keeping memory consumption low. Extensive experiments on the LIBERO benchmark show that our method significantly outperforms the baseline WoVR in terms of generalization, generation quality, robustness, fidelity, and the success rate of reinforcement-learning post-training for VLA models.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: VLA-GSE: Boosting Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning in VLA with Generalized and Specialized Experts
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yuhua Jiang, Junjie Lu, Xinyao Qin, Xiaoyu Chen, Kaixin Wang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: VLA-GSE enhances parameter-efficient fine-tuning for vision-language-action models by using generalized and specialized experts, improving robotic control adaptation while preserving pre-trained knowledge.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models inherit rich visual-semantic priors from pre-trained vision-language backbones, but adapting them to robotic control remains challenging. Full fine-tuning (FFT) is prone to overfitting on downstream robotic data and catastrophic forgetting of pretrained vision-language capabilities. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) better preserves pre-trained knowledge, yet existing PEFT methods still struggle to adapt effectively to robot control tasks. To address this gap, we propose VLA-GSE, a parameter-efficient VLA fine-tuning framework that improves control adaptation while retaining PEFT's knowledge preservation advantage. Specifically, VLA-GSE (Generalized and Specialized Experts) is initialized by spectrally decomposing the frozen backbone, assigning leading singular components to generalized experts (shared experts) and disjoint residual components to specialized experts (routed experts). This decomposition improves adaptation capacity under a fixed trainable-parameter budget. Under a comparable parameter budget, VLA-GSE updates only 2.51% of the full model parameters and consistently outperforms strong FFT and PEFT baselines. It achieves 81.2% average zero-shot success on LIBERO-Plus, preserves pre-trained VLM capability comparably to LoRA on multimodal understanding benchmarks, and improves real-world manipulation success under multiple distribution shifts. Code is available at: this https URL

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Beyond LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning: Gradient-Guided Optimizer Routing for LLM Adaptation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Haozhan Tang, Xiuqi Zhu, Xinyin Zhang, Boxun Li, Virginia Smith
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces Mixture of LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning (MoLF), a dynamic framework that optimally combines FFT and LoRA for improved large language model adaptation.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Recent literature on fine-tuning Large Language Models highlights a fundamental debate. While Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) provides the representational plasticity required for high-entropy knowledge injection, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can match or surpass FFT performance because many tasks only require updates in a low-rank space and benefit from LoRA's additional regularization. Through empirical evaluation across diverse tasks (SQL, Medical QA, and Counterfactual Knowledge) and varying language models (Gemma-3-1B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-3B), we verify both trends and demonstrate that relying solely on either static architecture is structurally limited. To address this challenge, we propose a Mixture of LoRA and Full (MoLF) Fine-Tuning, a unified framework that enables continuous navigation between both training regimes. MoLF dynamically routes updates between FFT and LoRA at the optimizer level to ensure that exact gradient signals are available to both experts throughout training, yielding stable training dynamics. For memory-constrained environments, we also introduce MoLF-Efficient, which freezes base weights and only routes updates among a pair of LoRA experts of potentially varying rank. Our evaluations show that MoLF either improves on or stays within $1.5\%$ of the better of FFT and LoRA across all settings, while MoLF-Efficient outperforms prior adaptive LoRA approaches by up to $20\%$ on Fact and $9\%$ on Med and SQL.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: AEM: Adaptive Entropy Modulation for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Haotian Zhao, Songlin Zhou, Yuxin Zhang, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Wenyu Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: AEM introduces a supervision-free method for credit assignment in multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning by adaptively modulating entropy dynamics, enhancing exploration-exploitation balance and improving performance across various tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the ability of large language model (LLM) agents to interact with environments and solve multi-turn tasks. However, effective agentic RL remains challenging: sparse outcome-only rewards provide limited guidance for assigning credit to individual steps within long interaction trajectories. Existing approaches often introduce dense intermediate supervision, such as process reward models or auxiliary self-supervised signals, which increases supervision and tuning complexity and may limit generalization across tasks and domains. We present AEM, a supervision-free credit assignment method that adaptively modulates entropy dynamics during RL training to improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off. Since in agentic RL the environment is typically affected by a complete response, rather than an individual token, our analysis lifts entropy dynamics from the token level to the response level, aligning uncertainty estimation with the effective action granularity of LLM agents and reducing sensitivity to token-level sampling noise. We further show that entropy drift under natural-gradient updates is governed by the interaction between the sampled-response advantage and its relative surprisal. Motivated by this result, AEM derives a practical response-level uncertainty proxy and uses it to rescale advantages, leveraging the evolving balance between positive and negative samples to naturally transition from exploration to exploitation. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SWE-bench-Verified with models ranging from 1.5B to 32B demonstrate that AEM consistently improves strong RL baselines, including a +1.4\% gain when integrated into a state-of-the-art software-engineering RL training framework.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Proxy3D: Efficient 3D Representations for Vision-Language Models via Semantic Clustering and Alignment
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jerry Jiang, Haowen Sun, Denis Gudovskiy, Yohei Nakata, Tomoyuki Okuno
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: Proxy3D introduces efficient 3D proxy representations for vision-language models, enhancing spatial consistency and performance in 3D visual tasks through semantic clustering and alignment.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence in vision-language models (VLMs) attracts research interest with the practical demand to reason in the 3D this http URL promising results, most existing methods follow the conventional 2D pipeline in VLMs and use pixel-aligned representations for the vision modality. However, correspondence-based models with implicit 3D scene understanding often fail to achieve spatial consistency, and representation-based models with 3D geometric priors lack efficiency in vision sequence serialization. To address this, we propose a Proxy3D method with compact yet comprehensive 3D proxy representations for the vision modality. Given only video frames as input, we employ semantic and geometric encoders to extract scene features and then perform their semantic-aware clustering to obtain a set of proxies in the 3D space. For representation alignment, we further curate the SpaceSpan dataset and apply multi-stage training to adopt the proposed 3D proxy representations with the VLM. When using shorter sequences for vision information, our method achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance in 3D visual question answering, visual grounding and general spatial intelligence benchmarks.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Towards Highly-Constrained Human Motion Generation with Retrieval-Guided Diffusion Noise Optimization
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Hanchao Liu, Fang-Lue Zhang, Shining Zhang, Tai-Jiang Mu, Shi-Min Hu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: This paper presents a retrieval-guided diffusion noise optimization method for generating human motion that effectively addresses complex spatiotemporal constraints without prior training.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Generating human motion that satisfies customized zero-shot goal functions, enabling applications such as controllable character animation and behavior synthesis for virtual agents, is a critical capability. A better initialization for diffusion noise is then obtained via a reward-guided mask that combines random noise with retrieved noise. By optimizing diffusion noise from this improved initialization, we successfully solve highly constrained generation tasks. By leveraging LLM for relational task parsing, the whole framework is further enabled to automatically reason for what to retrieve, improving the intelligence of moving agents under a training-free optimization scheme.

To overcome these limitations, we introduce Distribution Guided Policy Optimization, a novel critic free reinforcement learning framework that reinterprets distribution deviation as a guiding signal rather than a rigid penalty. DGPO replaces the volatile KL divergence with the bounded Hellinger distance to safely quantify token level exploration without the risk of gradient explosion. To effectively distinguish genuine reasoning breakthroughs from hallucinatory noise, we propose an entropy gating mechanism that scales this deviation by the policy`s epistemic uncertainty. By dynamically redistributing the coarse sequence-level advantage to individual tokens based on these gated scores, DGPO heavily incentivizes critical exploratory steps while suppressing unwarranted, low-entropy deviations. Consequently, DGPO completely eliminates the traditional token-level KL penalty and achieves fine-grained credit reallocation without the computational overhead of an additional value network. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that DGPO sets a new state-of-the-art for critic free alignment. Notably, on the Qwen2.5-32B architecture, DGPO achieves 60.0% Avg@32 accuracy and 46.0% Avg@32 accuracy on the challenging AIME2024 and AIME2025 benchmarks respectively, substantially outperforming competitive baselines like DAPO.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Sword: Style-Robust World Models as Simulators via Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping for VLA Policy Post-Training
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jiaxuan Gao, Yongjian Guo, Zhong Guan, Wen Huang, Wanlun Ma
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The Sword framework enhances World Models for Vision-Language-Action tasks by improving generalization and robustness through Structure-Guided Style Augmentation and Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: The integration of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with World Models has gained increasing attention. One representative approach treats learned World Models as generative simulators, enabling policy optimization entirely within "imagination." However, when deployed as simulators for specific environments such as the LIBERO benchmark, existing World Models often suffer from poor generalization and long-horizon error accumulation. During closed-loop rollouts, these models are highly sensitive to initial-state perturbations; minor changes in color, illumination, and other visual factors can trigger cascading hallucinations, leading to severe blurriness or overexposure. Moreover, long-horizon error accumulation further degrades the quality and fidelity of predicted future states. These issues limit the reliability of World Models as simulators. To mitigate these problems, we propose Sword, a robust World Model framework. Our method introduces Structure-Guided Style Augmentation to disentangle the visual textures of interactive environments from task-relevant dynamics, thereby improving generalization. We further propose Dynamic Latent Bootstrapping, which maintains consistency between training and inference while keeping memory consumption low. Extensive experiments on the LIBERO benchmark show that our method significantly outperforms the baseline WoVR in terms of generalization, generation quality, robustness, fidelity, and the success rate of reinforcement-learning post-training for VLA models.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: VLA-GSE: Boosting Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning in VLA with Generalized and Specialized Experts
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yuhua Jiang, Junjie Lu, Xinyao Qin, Xiaoyu Chen, Kaixin Wang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: VLA-GSE enhances parameter-efficient fine-tuning for vision-language-action models by using generalized and specialized experts, improving robotic control adaptation while preserving pre-trained knowledge.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models inherit rich visual-semantic priors from pre-trained vision-language backbones, but adapting them to robotic control remains challenging. Full fine-tuning (FFT) is prone to overfitting on downstream robotic data and catastrophic forgetting of pretrained vision-language capabilities. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) better preserves pre-trained knowledge, yet existing PEFT methods still struggle to adapt effectively to robot control tasks. To address this gap, we propose VLA-GSE, a parameter-efficient VLA fine-tuning framework that improves control adaptation while retaining PEFT's knowledge preservation advantage. Specifically, VLA-GSE (Generalized and Specialized Experts) is initialized by spectrally decomposing the frozen backbone, assigning leading singular components to generalized experts (shared experts) and disjoint residual components to specialized experts (routed experts). This decomposition improves adaptation capacity under a fixed trainable-parameter budget. Under a comparable parameter budget, VLA-GSE updates only 2.51% of the full model parameters and consistently outperforms strong FFT and PEFT baselines. It achieves 81.2% average zero-shot success on LIBERO-Plus, preserves pre-trained VLM capability comparably to LoRA on multimodal understanding benchmarks, and improves real-world manipulation success under multiple distribution shifts.
